tldr_label: TL;DR: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang under Trump pressure and Wall Street posts its best day since April 2025, NATO sends AWACS to Poland, and Ukraine strikes

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, and the stock jumped about 31%. Lawmakers in both parties condemned the move, and Democrats vowed investigations. [[TAG:warning:backlash]]

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: The S&P 500 rose 4.7% and the Nasdaq 6.5% on Monday. Asia surged Tuesday, but US futures slipped as chip stocks cooled. [[TAG:success:relief rally]]

tldr_bullets.label: NATO
tldr_bullets.body: An extraordinary North Atlantic Council met on Poland as NATO deployed AWACS aircraft. Poland reported another Russian drone incursion. [[TAG:warning:eastern flank]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Zelensky said Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya. The Kremlin warned of painful consequences. [[TAG:danger:war widens]]

tldr_bullets.label: Climate
tldr_bullets.body: Guterres called COP31's failure deeply disappointing. Technical decisions survived, and talks move to COP32 next year. [[TAG:info:aftermath]]

sections.title: Nvidia: Huang Reinstated
sections.summary: Board unanimously restores Huang as CEO after Trump push; Congress erupts

paragraphs.heading: The Reversal
paragraphs.body: Nvidia said its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and board director, effective immediately, and that it was satisfied with his candor. The company said its independent investigation into a foreign intelligence effort targeting him will continue. CNBC reported that Trump said he sealed the deal and that the board sought guarantees Huang was not a security threat. Fox Business described the move as following US government input. PBS called Huang chairman, while Nvidia's release says Harvey Jones remains board chair. [[TAG:warning:probe continues]]

paragraphs.heading: Capitol Hill
paragraphs.body: Axios, CNBC and PBS reported bipartisan backlash, with lawmakers moving ahead with hearings. Semafor reported lawmakers are unconvinced by the administration's claim that Huang poses no national security risk. MS NOW reported that Republican Sen. John Cornyn questioned the official assurances. CNN reported the stock soared about 30% on the news. [[TAG:danger:bipartisan anger]]

sections.title: Markets: Best Day Since 2025
sections.summary: S&P 500 up 4.7%, Nasdaq 6.5%; Asia surges Tuesday as US futures cool

paragraphs.heading: Monday's Rally
paragraphs.body: Yahoo Finance reported the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted their best day since April 2025 as Nvidia soared on Huang's return. CNBC reported the Nasdaq rose about 6.5%. Cappnotes reported the S&P 500 gained 4.73% to 7,237.17 and the Dow rose about 1,448 points to 49,595.31; 24/7 Wall St. put the S&P close slightly higher, at 7,243.94. [[TAG:success:relief rally]]

paragraphs.heading: Tuesday
paragraphs.body: Kotak Neo and NewsBytes reported Korea's Kospi up about 7.5%, Japan's Nikkei up about 5% after a holiday, and Taiwan up about 9%, all intraday figures. TipRanks, Invezz and Rallies reported US futures slipping as chip stocks cooled, with Nasdaq-100 futures down about 1%. Invezz cited renewed congressional scrutiny of Nvidia. Investors are awaiting PCE inflation data. [[TAG:warning:fragile]]

sections.title: NATO: AWACS Over Poland
sections.summary: Extraordinary council meets; AWACS deployed; Poland reports a new drone incursion

paragraphs.heading: Council Session
paragraphs.body: HNGN and AeroTime reported that NATO deployed AWACS early-warning aircraft to Poland, and HNGN said NATO holds Russia fully responsible. Around Prague reported the North Atlantic Council met on Poland as the aircraft reinforced its airspace, and that Rutte said it is still unclear whether the missiles crossed in deliberately. Poland did not invoke Article 4. [[TAG:info:AWACS]]

paragraphs.heading: Diplomacy and a New Incursion
paragraphs.body: News.az reported Poland would summon Russia's ambassador over the missile breach. Reports conflict on whether the summons has happened yet. Newscord reported a fresh Russian drone intrusion that prompted an air alarm and sheltering orders in the Lublin region. [[TAG:warning:new breach]]

sections.title: Ukraine: Strike in Libya
sections.summary: Ukraine says naval drones sank Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi; Kremlin warns

paragraphs.heading: Benghazi
paragraphs.body: ABC News, CBS News and NBC News reported Zelensky's confirmation that Ukrainian naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury and damaged a sanctioned cargo ship off Libya. RFE/RL reported the strike near Benghazi. Al Jazeera's explainer noted that Libyan officials first described the warship as badly damaged, and Russia has not confirmed the loss. [[TAG:danger:war widens]]

paragraphs.heading: Kremlin and Context
paragraphs.body: Reports said Kremlin spokesman Peskov called the attacks a very dangerous trend and warned of painful consequences. IBTimes reported the strike sparked a sovereignty dispute with Libyan authorities. Earlier this month, US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced no breakthrough, Time reported. [[TAG:warning:escalation]]

sections.title: Climate: After Antalya
sections.summary: Guterres laments COP31 failure; technical decisions survive; COP32 next

paragraphs.heading: Guterres
paragraphs.body: UN News reported Guterres said he was deeply disappointed that COP31 ended without consensus but that there is no ambiguity in the science. A second UN News report covered him urging climate justice from Barbados. JURIST reported the talks collapsed over fossil fuel commitments. [[TAG:warning:setback]]

paragraphs.heading: What Survives
paragraphs.body: Reports said parties still adopted technical decisions on a just transition, finance and adaptation, and will reconvene at COP32. Gulf News examined what the failure means for global climate action. Audacy, carrying AP, reported experts see reform pressure and some momentum on phasing out fossil fuels. [[TAG:info:COP32 next]]

sections.title: Iran: Pressure Without Strikes
sections.summary: Trump defers strikes to the new year as Treasury adds sanctions; Bahrain hit

paragraphs.heading: Washington
paragraphs.body: Khaleej Times reported Trump delayed potential Iran strikes until the new year, and Fox News reported he hinted at new strikes in 2027. CFR's tracker reported new Treasury sanctions on eight individuals and 22 businesses supporting Iran. Benzinga reported Bessent unveiled fresh sanctions as Tehran warned tankers against using Hormuz. [[TAG:info:deferred]]

paragraphs.heading: Tehran and the Gulf
paragraphs.body: FDD's overnight brief and Just Security's early edition tracked Iran's vow to confront the US naval blockade. GlobalSecurity noted a lull of several days in direct US-Iran strikes, alongside unconfirmed tanker mine claims. Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility and injured two. [[TAG:warning:blockade]]

sections.title: Also Watching
sections.summary: Eisenkot eyes a surprise vote; UNRWA worker killed in Gaza; Africa's energy windfall

paragraphs.heading: Israel and Gaza
paragraphs.body: The Times of Israel and ANI reported Eisenkot is planning to declare a coalition at a surprise moment and call a quick Knesset vote to limit defections, after Al Jazeera reported weekend talks with Likud ended without a deal. Democracy Now reported Israeli attacks in Gaza killed Palestinians delivering aid and an UNRWA worker. [[TAG:warning:minority bid]]

paragraphs.heading: Africa and Latin America
paragraphs.body: OkayAfrica reported that nine African energy exporters earned an extra $21.6 billion from higher prices during the Iran war, and that Kenya and DR Congo agreed to restore ambassadors. The Rio Times reported Brazil's lower house approved the base text of a fiscal adjustment bill. [[TAG:info:regional]]
